commit.message:
refresh github credentials only right before it will expire (#16803)

## Description
Reduce repeated GitHub credential requests for restricted runs whose
credential response contains only GitHub credentials. These requests can
repeatedly resolve repository scope and consume the shared GitHub
installation API quota.

- Refresh ten minutes before the returned expiry, capped at fifty
minutes and with a one-minute minimum interval.
- Save a monotonic deadline when credentials are accepted and publish it
only after credential files are written successfully. Setup time counts
toward the deadline.
- Keep the existing one-minute schedule for mixed-forge and empty
responses. Non-GitHub credentials do not yet provide expiry values.
- Keep credential clearing on refresh failure, task isolation, and
legacy credential behavior unchanged. Failed refreshes return to the
one-minute retry interval.

This is a client-only change. It does not add server changes, cross-run
credential sharing, or separate forge timers.

## Linked Issue
None.

## Testing
- Added deterministic regression tests for expiry bounds, mixed-forge
fallback, elapsed setup time, overdue deadlines, failed writes and
clears, recovery, and task isolation.
- Tests were not run, at the user's request. The targeted test command
was cancelled.
- Clippy and build checks were not run before publishing.
- `./script/format` completed successfully.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Read-only code review found no material issues.
